projects.title: Making Sense of Credit Access
projects.summary: Building decision systems that help match borrowers with the right lending opportunities.
projects.intro: Getting a loan isn't simply a question of whether someone is creditworthy. It also depends on whether they need credit, how much they need, and which lender might serve them. I worked on bringing these questions together into a more useful decision framework.

sections.title: Beyond Credit Scores
sections.text: Developed a framework combining credit eligibility, borrowing propensity, expected loan size and lender affinity. Rather than treating every customer as a generic lead, the system helps identify the most appropriate lending or credit-improvement journey.

sections.title: Finding the Right Borrowers
sections.text: Built a personal-loan prioritization model. On out-of-time validation, a segment representing roughly 40% of applications accounted for 80% of disbursals and 90% of high-ticket disbursals.

projects.title: Reimagining Business Analytics with AI
projects.summary: Moving from traditional reporting towards a world where people can ask questions directly of their data.
projects.intro: Most organizations have plenty of data but still depend on analysts to answer everyday business questions. I've been working on changing that by combining faster analytical infrastructure with open-source AI tools.

sections.title: Rethinking the Data Warehouse
sections.text: Led the migration of analytical workloads from PostgreSQL to ClickHouse. A proof of concept reduced one representative query from 31 seconds to 0.8 seconds, demonstrating the potential for substantially faster reporting and exploration.

sections.title: Analytics Through Conversation
sections.text: Building a self-service analytics layer using LibreChat and domain-specific AI agents. The idea is to let business teams investigate performance, explore trends and query the warehouse through natural-language conversations.

projects.title: Finding Fraud in Names
projects.summary: Using language similarity and machine learning to uncover potentially fraudulent loan applications.
projects.intro: A person's name can appear differently across documents and banking records. Sometimes that's harmless. Sometimes those inconsistencies reveal something worth investigating. At TVS Credit, I worked on using these variations as signals for fraud detection.

sections.title: When Names Don't Match
sections.text: Developed NLP-based identity-matching workflows to compare customer information against banking records. Used fuzzy matching and machine learning to distinguish ordinary naming variations from suspicious discrepancies.

sections.title: Turning Patterns into Risk Signals
sections.text: Integrated identity-matching signals into fraud-identification workflows for consumer-durable lending. The initiative contributed to identifying approximately ₹35 crore in potential fraud risk during FY24.
